# Live dashboard — runbook

Private operating view at `/dashboard`. Danielle keeps one Google Sheet up to date;
everything else follows from it.

```
Danielle ──▶ Google Sheet ──▶ /api/dashboard ──▶ /dashboard
             (data entry)      (token-gated,      (charts)
                                5-min cache)
```

## The sheet

**Doña Fuego — Live Data**, in the `Dona Distillery` Drive folder. Generated by
`tools/build_live_data_workbook.py`; re-run it to rebuild the blank workbook.

| Tab | Who touches it | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `1 Checkers Emails` | Danielle, weekly | The Checkers "Sales (Last Week: …)" email, pasted at the bottom |
| `2 Checkers Sales Out` | only if the email format changes | Hand-typed weeks; overrides the parsed value for the same week and SKU |
| `3 DC Sales In` | Danielle, per order | Our invoices to Checkers |
| `4 Cost of Sales` | occasionally | Actual cost per case for the six pro forma lines |
| `5 Bulk Allocation` | occasionally | Total allocation, litres per case, draws |
| `6 Assumptions` | rarely | Shelf prices, units per case, wholesale price, plan months |

The sheet holds **no formulas** — Drive's xlsx import drops them, and the same
arithmetic is easier to test in JavaScript. All computation happens in
`api/_lib/transform.js`.

Weekly job, in full: open the email, select all, copy, paste at the bottom of tab 1.
Pasting a thread that quotes earlier weeks is harmless — weeks already recorded are
ignored.

## Configuration

Vercel project → Settings → Environment Variables:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `SHEET_ID` | The id in the sheet URL, `/spreadsheets/d/<SHEET_ID>/edit` |
| `GOOGLE_SA_EMAIL` | Service-account address, `…@….iam.gserviceaccount.com` |
| `GOOGLE_SA_PRIVATE_KEY` | The `private_key` from the service-account JSON, newlines and all |
| `DASHBOARD_TOKEN` | The access key. Long and random — this is the only thing guarding live cost and margin data |

Creating the service account, once:

1. Google Cloud console → new project (or an existing one) → enable the **Google Sheets API**.
2. IAM → Service Accounts → create one → Keys → Add key → JSON.
3. Copy `client_email` into `GOOGLE_SA_EMAIL` and `private_key` into `GOOGLE_SA_PRIVATE_KEY`.
4. Share the sheet with that `client_email` address, **Viewer** is enough.

The dashboard is then reached at `/dashboard?key=<DASHBOARD_TOKEN>`. The key is held in
`sessionStorage` for the rest of the browser session; it is never written to the page.

Rotating the key: change `DASHBOARD_TOKEN` in Vercel and redeploy. Old links stop working
immediately.

## Why the gate is real

`/dataroom` hides content that is already in the shipped HTML — obscurity, not security.
`/dashboard` is different: without a valid token `/api/dashboard` returns `401` and no
data, so cost of sales, margin and allocation never reach an unauthorised browser.

## Testing

```
node tools/test-transform.js      # 51 checks, incl. the real Checkers email
node tools/dev-server.js          # serves site/ with fixture data on :4321
                                  # -> http://localhost:4321/dashboard?key=local-dev-key
```

`api/_lib/demo-data.js` carries an invented ramp in the real email's format, so the local
view matches production shape without putting trading figures in a public repository.

## Sample mode

The review project `donadashboard` runs with no sheet behind it and serves
`api/_lib/demo-data.js` instead, flagged `sample: true` and banded in red on the page.
Sample mode skips the token gate, so that hostname is **public** — every figure in
`demo-data.js` must therefore be invented. Never paste reported sell-through into it.
It needs both an unconfigured sheet **and** the review project's own hostname, so sample
figures cannot reach the investor site whatever its configuration.

```
SAMPLE=1 node tools/dev-server.js     # same path locally, on :4321
```

## Known gaps

- **Shelf price** is R42.25 a can (R169 incl VAT for a 4-pack, per Checkers). Change it on the
  Assumptions tab if Checkers reprices — cases, cover and the plan comparison all key off it.
- **Week ending 9 August is inferred.** The email that reported it carried no date header.
- **The annualised run rate** extrapolates a launch ramp, so it reads high while the
  initial fill is still selling through. The label names its four-week basis.
